content: Before starting fluconazole, it is important to read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This should also be reviewed each time you receive a refill. In Canada, some brands of this medication may be available without a prescription. The effects of fluconazole can last for several days after taking it. Common side effects of fluconazole include nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, and dizziness. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Rarely, fluconazole can cause serious liver disease or severe allergic reactions. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the U.S., you can also call 1-800-222-1222 for poison control, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Before taking fluconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungal drugs (such as ketoconazole or itraconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Fluconazole may also cause a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart rhythm. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions, are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation, or have low levels of potassium or magnesium in your blood. This risk may also be heightened by the use of diuretics (water pills) or conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Although uncommon, fluconazole may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Limit alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. During pregnancy, fluconazole should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby if taken during the first three months of pregnancy. Fluconazole does pass into breast milk, but it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how fluconazole or other medications work, or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Fluconazole can slow the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. Store fluconazole at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about fluconazole. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
